request: We have a loop in a notebook that keeps calling the model until it decides it is finished. It works on my laptop. Next month real customers hit it. What has to change before that?
source: authored
note: Catches a prototype-to-runtime hardening request being answered as framework choice instead of loop-contract work.

request: Our refund flow stops and waits for a manager, sometimes for two days, and the downstream call retries on its own. How do we build that so a restart does not lose or double anything?
source: routing-checklist RT-04: 'Known approval process with pauses and retries'
note: Catches an approval-wait-and-restart request being routed to durable-state or multi-agent modules instead of the pause/resume procedure. The boundary set excludes the primary by convention: HRN-02 is what the pause/resume clause activates and it is already the expected primary here.

request: We want a research assistant and a compliance reviewer working the same case at the same time, and neither may see the other's notes. Is that even worth doing?
source: routing-checklist RT-13: 'Parallel specialists with separate confidential context'
note: Ambiguous by construction: HRN-03 (add collaboration to a loop) vs ARC-03 (more than one participant); the request asks whether to add collaborators to an existing loop, so HRN-03 is primary per the tools/memory/handoffs router row, while ARC-03 still fires as a compound boundary because more than one agent participates.

request: The assistant times out waiting on our charge-card endpoint and then calls it again. Twice now a customer got billed twice. We were going to add 'do not retry' to the prompt.
source: routing-checklist RT-05: 'Agent repeatedly calls a write tool after timeout'; must not load prompt-only fix
note: Catches the prompt-only fix attractor and a missed pause/resume boundary on a retried effect.

request: A vendor gave us a hosted connector endpoint so the assistant can pull our customers' invoices. Their docs say it speaks the standard protocol, so we should be able to just point at it.
source: routing-checklist RT-12: 'Connect a remote MCP server with user data'; must not treat protocol compatibility as authorization
note: Catches protocol compatibility being accepted as authorization, and routing to framework selection instead of the protocol/identity contract.

request: The assistant should remember that this user always wants metric units, and also what we agreed in last week's session, and the facts it looked up about their account. Right now it all goes in one table.
source: authored
note: Catches durable memory being answered as a retrieval/index problem instead of separated stores with owner, scope, expiry and deletion.

request: We run fifteen copies of the same analyst and take whatever most of them say. They all read the same three source documents. Fifteen agreeing feels like strong evidence.
source: routing-checklist RT-26: shared evidence may make the majority wrong together; must not treat majority count as a truth guarantee
note: Catches correlated-evidence voting being scored as a judge/agreement problem and a missed ARC-03 boundary.

request: Late in a long run one test proved an assumption from step two wrong. Most of the work after that is still fine. We do not want to start the whole thing over every time this happens.
source: routing-checklist RT-28: 'A late test invalidates one early assumption while most completed work remains usable'
note: Catches selective invalidation and replay being answered as a global restart or as a coding-agent workflow.

request: After a node restart two workers picked up the same payout job and both wrote the ledger row. What is the right shape so that cannot happen?
source: authored
note: Catches duplicated concurrent effects being routed to runtime/deployment advice instead of ownership, leases and idempotency contracts.

request: We want the assistant to work in our main service repo on its own overnight and leave pull requests for us in the morning.
source: routing-checklist RT-09: 'Agent should modify this repository safely'; must not answer with a generic code-generation prompt
note: Catches repository-mutating autonomy being answered as prompt engineering.

request: Before one of those generated diffs actually ships, what do we need to have checked and who signs it?
source: routing-checklist RT-09 second half: 'Approve or release generated code'
note: Catches a code-release gate being escalated into regulated-domain controls when no regulated regime or official record was mentioned.

request: We have about four thousand internal policy PDFs on a share drive, different templates, some scanned. We want the assistant to be able to use them.
source: routing-checklist RT-06: 'Answer private policy questions with citations'; must not make fine-tuning the first step
note: Catches corpus ingestion being answered with fine-tuning, the most common wrong first step for private documents.

request: Every answer has to show the exact paragraph it came from, and someone in Germany must not get an answer built from the US-only policy.
source: routing-checklist RT-06: citations plus private-policy access
note: Catches per-request evidence and authorization being dropped in favour of generic retrieval quality tuning.

request: People ask things like which of our suppliers are ultimately owned by the same parent company. Similarity search just returns paragraphs that use the same words.
source: routing-checklist RT-07: 'Reason across ownership relationships and paths'; must not assume vector-only
note: Catches multi-hop relationship questions staying in vector-only retrieval, or being diverted into graph-algorithm or training modules.

request: Product search misses when someone types the exact part number, good hits land on page three, and nobody here knows how many shards we should have.
source: routing-checklist RT-08: 'Tune hybrid search relevance and shard design'; must not load a general agent loop
note: Catches a search-engine tuning request being turned into an agent design.

request: Six weeks of prompt work and retrieval and the output still drifts off our house format. The team wants to start training on our own examples.
source: routing-checklist RT-20: 'Prompting and RAG still cannot produce a stable domain format; should we tune?'
note: Ambiguous by construction: PRM-02 (diagnose prompt failure) vs MOD-01 (choose the adaptation layer); the request asks which layer to move to after prompting and retrieval were already tried, which is MOD-01's trigger, and the router sends 'choose prompt, RAG, SFT, LoRA...' there, so MOD-01 wins and the prompt module is the attractor.

request: We are pulling five thousand resolved support tickets to train on. Two annotators disagree a lot, and the same issue shows up in tickets from several months.
source: routing-checklist RT-20/RT-21: build training/preference data
note: Catches training-data construction being answered as evaluation-set construction, and misses on leakage-aware splitting and rights/provenance.

request: Can we get away with adapters on a small open model instead of retraining the whole thing, and how do we back it out if it turns out worse?
source: routing-checklist RT-20: fine-tuning without held-out evidence is the failure
note: Catches the rollback wording pulling release-operations instead of the adaptation choice with baselines and a reversible canary.

request: We have thumbs up and down on individual tool calls, plus unit tests that pass or fail. Can the model learn to pick tools better from that signal?
source: routing-checklist RT-21: 'Improve tool behavior from preference or verifiable reward data'; must not allow unconstrained online self-training
note: Catches preference/verifiable-reward training being answered as coding-agent work, and misses the constraints-outside-reward requirement.

request: Before we launch the internal-docs assistant we need to agree how we will know if it is any good.
source: routing-checklist RT-32: 'Design an evaluation plan for this RAG system'; must not auto-execute benchmarks
note: Catches an eval plan turning into benchmark execution, or a jump to fine-tuning before anything is measured. judge-bias-and-calibration.md is deliberately NOT forbidden: a router row naming EVA-01 loads it, so forbidding it would penalise the shipped route.

request: The new version lands on the same final answers as the old one but it wanders around a lot more getting there. How should we compare the two?
source: routing-checklist RT-10: 'Compare two agent versions beyond final answer'; must not reduce to one aggregate judge score
note: Catches trajectory comparison collapsing into a single aggregate judge score.

request: What does precision at ten actually tell me, and when is it the wrong number to be looking at?
source: routing-checklist RT-31: 'Explain precision@k and when to use it'; must not do a full readiness review or run benchmarks
note: Catches a bare metric explanation escalating into a readiness review, a judge build, or a retrieval redesign.

request: We want the model to rate our generated release notes one to five for clarity, and the pipeline should stop the release if it comes back under three.
source: routing-checklist RT-11: 'Use an LLM to grade subjective proposal quality'; must not claim deterministic equivalence
note: Catches a model score wired to a numeric release gate without the judge-calibration boundary firing.

request: Here are the forty cases we agreed on and the staging deployment they should run against. Please run them and tell me what broke.
source: routing-checklist RT-33: 'Run the supplied evaluation cases against this endpoint'; a plan-only reply is the failure when artifacts and authority are present
note: Catches an explicit, authorized execution request being answered with a plan only. judge-bias-and-calibration.md is deliberately NOT forbidden: a router row naming EVA-01 loads it.

request: In our test helper, rename the variable `resp` to `response` in the three places it appears in that one file.
source: authored
note: Negative: a fixed low-risk mechanical edit. Plausible attractor is the coding-agent module because the words 'test' and 'file' appear; loading it here is the bloat failure.

request: I have a twelve-row CSV with a fixed header. Sum the third column and print the total.
source: authored
note: Negative: deterministic one-step task with no model in it. Attractors are the data/RAG module (because 'CSV') and the eval module (because 'total'); either load means the proportional-execution rule is not held.

request: Quick one: is temperature just another name for top_p?
source: authored
note: Negative: bare one-line concept question answerable directly. Attractors are the prompt/context module and the training module; loading either turns a one-sentence answer into a procedure run.
